text:
UTA comes into Seattle on two days' rest after a 5-4 win over Pittsburgh, a Penguins team now winless in four. The Mammoth are 4-1-0 in their last five and without Michael Carcone, though John Marino is day-to-day and could return. SEA played Tuesday, beating Detroit 4-3 in a shootout in a game where Alex DeBrincat reached 300 career goals. The Kraken are 3-1-1 in their last five, without Jacob Melanson and Ryan Lindgren, and the story here is a Kraken team whose results are running ahead of its play.

That gap shows in the chances. At five on five, UTA has taken 57% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality) in its games, SEA 46%. SEA's goal difference of +3 sits on -5.0 expected, and finishing is doing the lifting. UTA has the better power play, but it takes 4.3 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Karel Vejmelka (UTA) and Joey Daccord (SEA) are both below expected this season, -1.3 and -2.3 goals saved above expected. Last season Vejmelka was at +5.4, Daccord at -6.1. Our model has UTA at 3.37 expected goals tonight, SEA at 2.77.

Players to watch: Nick Schmaltz (34% to score, 68% for a point) and Dylan Guenther (34% to score) lead UTA, while Jared McCann (29% to score) tops SEA's power play. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Anders Lee, a third-liner at about 14 minutes a night who has 4.1 expected goals in his last 10 games and 9 high-danger shots, against a Kraken defense that allows plenty. Ryan Winterton plays his 100th NHL game for SEA, as does Nick DeSimone for UTA.
